name: College Move-In Checklist
description: A step-by-step checklist for a smooth college move-in day.

items.text: Confirm your assigned move-in date and time window.
Review parking, traffic and unloading instructions.
items.note: Many schools enforce strict time slots — plan to arrive on time.

items.text: Map your route and a backup in case of closures.
Coordinate large or shared items with your roommate.
Label every box with your name and room number.
Charge your phone and any devices the night before.
Load heavy and bulky items into the vehicle first.
Keep your first-night box easy to reach.
Bring a hand truck or dolly if you have one.
Pack a small toolkit for assembling furniture.
Bring water, snacks and comfortable shoes.
Keep documents and keys in a bag with you.
Arrive within your assigned move-in window.
Check in and pick up your room key or access card.
Collect any move-in packet or paperwork.
Note where to park and the unloading time limit.
Locate elevators, stairs and the nearest entrance.
Find out where move-in carts are available.
Unload the vehicle quickly to free the spot.
Move heavy items first while energy is high.
Stage boxes in the room before unpacking.
Keep walkways and doorways clear for others.
Have a helper guard items during trips.
Break down empty boxes and recycle them.
Make the bed first so you can rest later.
Set up your desk and charge your devices.
Unpack toiletries and your first-night essentials.
Arrange storage and put clothes away.
Test electronics, outlets and the internet.
Add a few personal touches to feel at home.
Complete the room condition or inventory form.
items.note: Document existing damage to protect your deposit.

items.text: Photograph any damage you find on arrival.
Save housing, RA and maintenance contacts.
Confirm your meal plan and ID card work.
Note quiet hours, laundry and trash rules.
Say goodbye to family and attend any welcome events.

faq.q: What should I do before college move-in day?
faq.a: Confirm your move-in time slot, map out parking and your route, label your boxes by destination, and pack a first-night essentials bag. Handling logistics in advance prevents most move-in day stress.

It's a single box or bag with everything you'll need the first night before fully unpacking: bedding, toiletries, a phone charger, medications, a change of clothes and basic snacks. Keep it easy to reach.

faq.q: How long does college move-in take?
faq.a: Unloading often takes one to two hours depending on parking, elevators and crowds, while full setup can take a day. Arriving early in your window usually means shorter lines.

faq.q: Can my family help me move in?
faq.a: Usually yes, though some schools limit how many helpers or vehicles are allowed at once. Check your move-in instructions so everyone knows the rules before arriving.

faq.q: Can I download this checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the checklist or download the PDF and tick off each step as you move through move-in day.
